items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: I stood in Pierron's band until he broke up the old band in 1932

ctx.x: And how long did you stay with that band?

Well I just played the job with him, I went back to my band. I see, yes. I stood in Pierron's band until he broke up the old band in 1932, then he took over a band they called the Sonny South. Uh-huh.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: that's where I went, P-Rong Band. All that was in 1928. And I worked in that band a good while.

ctx.x: Yeah. That was during the time when, uh, when Paul Bobberin, we left P-Rong Band to go with a kid, uh, Sonny Allen. Uh-huh. I mean, with, uh, Sonny Allen and them and Walter P. Sean, that's where I went, P-Rong Band. All that was in 1928. And I worked in that band a good while.
That was after you made that recording, was it? Yeah, it was way after.

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: But when I went in the band, would have been 30, let me see, no, 28. They was wearing, we was wearing, you know, what you call like a gamel of striped pants

ctx.x: But now, Celestan and Pirone's band, you played with them. Yeah, them guys were uniform. What were they dressed like?

Well, Pirone band, before I went in that group, they was, I think, now they're uniformed, I don't know if they were tuxedos when they were working at Tranchino. But when I went in the band, would have been 30, let me see, no, 28. They was wearing, we was wearing, you know, what you call like a gamel of striped pants, and sort of a pants, sort of a checkered coat like. Like pep and salt coat, with gamel of striped pants when we were working at Suburban Garden nightclub. And then a tuxedo band, well they always…
Well, did those high class people like the Lone Iron Blues and the barrel-ass?
